model_scope_leaps.statement: 0.886 sqrt(l) is the heuristic negation-rho constant.
The rho running time quoted everywhere (including standards) is this heuristic; worst case is unbounded.
SEC 1's step counts (sqrt(pi n/4), Table 2 MIPS-years) are the heuristic rho constants.
Half-bit-length strength is the square-root rho cost.
The (1.253 + o(1)) sqrt r cost used for implemented DP rho is Theorem 14.2.16 under Heuristic 14.2.15.
Implemented EC rho uses r-adding walks; its sqrt(pi r/2) cost is the random-walk constant times the Teske/Brent-Pollard factor, both heuristic.
The familiar square-root cost and leading birthday constant depend on the random-walk model.
Distinguished endpoints make many walkers contribute to one collision process.
Orbit folding supplies the conventional square-root constant-factor estimate.

route_closures_on_weak_support.statement: With classes the 2-cycle rate is 1/(N_C n_S) per step, so fruitless cycles appear regularly unless handled; the theorem ignores them.
4-cycles at Theta(1/r^2) are not handled by the Wiener-Zuccherato rule, so walks cycle within Theta(r^2) steps.
Without a subspace the extension-field relation-search route is unavailable, which is why the prime case has no algorithm with a cost estimate.
Semaev's naive method with a dense factor-base polynomial cannot beat generic methods when solved by Gröbner bases (conditionally).
An assumption that bounds the solving degree by a constant first fall degree regardless of the number of variables would decide an NP-complete problem in polynomial time.
No linearized QSP makes the QSP algorithm beat generic algorithms under its own cost estimate.
Split linearized trinomials beat brute force but not generic algorithms.
For prime N in [160, 600] the GHS construction yields no useful cover.
Asymptotically, (g)GHS is almost never faster than the best non-descent solver.
Few small-height points in E~(Q) force exponentially large lifts of random points (heuristic).
Under bounded rank, no lift of a growing number of random points to bounded height exists.
Simultaneously lifted points are almost never dependent, so xedni rarely yields a relation.
Kosters-Yeo: an unrestricted first-fall-degree assumption would decide an NP-complete evaluation problem; Nagao's estimate assumes the same first-fall behaviour.
No base size, table fold or target generator inside the pair-table two-summand family reaches rho at any size that matters.
The natural lifted index calculus is estimated to be slower than brute force.
Bounded dependence coefficients make a random reduced tuple useful with only order-1/p probability under the theorem's assumptions.

live_obstructions.statement: A degree-of-regularity predictor fails on ECDLP relation systems.
Substituting i_reg(F^top) halves the true solving degree on ECDLP relation systems.
First fall degree can be arbitrarily below or above sd, last fall, d_reg and reg, even with field equations.
On descended S_3 the first fall degree is 2 at every n while the measured degree of regularity grows.
In general D_ff carries no information about the maximal degree reached.
D_ff stays 2 while the degree reached grows with n at m = 2.
At m = 2, D_ff = 2 and D_reg rises from 4 to 5 between n = 36 and 37, i.e. D_reg - D_ff is not o(1)-close at fixed value and is moving with n.
Degree 5 measured at n = 45, m = t = 2 where the first fall degree is 2: the degree reached is not first fall + o(1).
Fixed-size Boolean systems at large n cannot be semi-regular, so semi-regular d_reg is not their degree.
Even with F^top semi-regular, sd = d_reg + 1.
With field equations sd exceeds d_reg by 8-9 degrees.
On index-calculus decomposition systems d_reg under-predicts sd (4 vs 5).
On index-calculus systems d_reg is undefined and i_reg(F^top) = 8 vs sd = 15.
For Weil restrictions the BFS d_reg is known exactly and grows linearly with the extension degree.

A published reading of degree 5 at n = 45, m = t = 2 on the diagonal with Semaev's subspace contradicts d_F4 <= 4 if KY's step degree equals Semaev's d_F4; not a committed certificate (repository S6 keeps the off-diagonal failure NOT established).
The spectral argument relies on the squaring branch; Miller-Venkatesan note mixing would be exponential in log n without it.
Quadratic growth of h gives no uniform lower-bound constant; the JKSST Lean audit has an explicit scaled-lattice countermodel.
The measured rate follows the exact count 16 C(|F|,6)/l, not the asymptotic 1/(ng)!; small bases are 3-30% below the asymptotic rate.
Constant-degree arms for binary descent (as in the ECC2K-130 FFDA projection) contradict the published growth of the degree of regularity with n at m = 2 (KY, up to n = 45).
Heuristic constant sqrt(pi/2) = 1.2533 vs proved 52.5: the rigorous result confirms the order but leaves a ~42x gap in the constant.
Semaev closure degrees stay at or below 4 through m=6 at toy sizes, one below semi-regular controls; the study states this is not evidence about the first fall degree assumption.
FFD is 2 (m=2) and 3 (m=3) on every toy system while the solving degree diverges, which the cryptanalysis synthesis reads as refuting the FFD assumption 'as stated'.
The rigorous bridge from a degree to solver cost goes through the last fall degree and the GB degree, not the first fall degree.
NP-completeness of summation-polynomial evaluation (under the authors' assumption) means no first-fall bound can carry a general polynomial-cost estimate.
On ECC2K-130 the transfer target exceeds 1.3e9 bits, so MOV/FR is not a route there.
On supersingular curves in fixed characteristic the transfer lands in a field where Kleinjung-Wesolowski prove quasi-polynomial DLP.
Makes the footprint heuristic's conclusion rigorous with sharp lead constants, in the random-selection model.
The m! invariant-coordinate gain survives Weil descent only when V^(i) stays l-dimensional; otherwise variables grow, which applies to F_(2^n), n prime (no proper subfield except F_2).
Rigorous partition-walk results exist (survey: Kijima-Montenegro, Montenegro et al.), narrowing but not removing the heuristic.
Same phenomenon in characteristic 2: a constant first fall degree that does not track the solver degree.

Diem needs no zero-dimensionality hypothesis: his algorithm lists only isolated solutions and he proves a q^(-1/2) fraction of points have an isolated decomposition (for (2+eps)n^2 <= log2 q). The hypothesis is needed only for the heuristic 1/n! yield and solver-cost analyses.
For elliptic curves over F_{q^n} with log2 q >= 7n, Condition 2.7 plus the genus bound prove what Gaudry assumes (irreducibility and ~q points).
The descent heuristics as originally stated are problematic in the non-Kummer case; patched versions are still heuristic.
GKZ's descent removes the smoothness heuristics, proving quasi-polynomial time where the representation exists.
Gives proved solving-degree bounds for systems whose F^h is verified semi-regular and in generic coordinates; the heuristic is needed only where semi-regularity is assumed rather than checked.
d_reg rigorously bounds only the output degree, not the degree the computation reaches.
Replaces 'sd ~ d_reg' by the proved sd <= d_reg + 1 for reinsertion algorithms when d_reg is finite.
Proves the affine and homogeneous computations agree below d_reg when F^top is semi-regular, identifies the y-torsion that breaks the heuristic, and gives 2D-1/2D-2 bounds.
Improves m^2 + 1 to m^2 - m + 1 for m >= 3.
Independent reproduction of the same degree values (5 at |V| = 2^9, 6 at 2^10) in a different regime (fixed 31-bit p, inconsistent targets), with a different engine.
Curves over F_{p^6} with order divisible by 4 that walk to the weak class fall below rho in the harness from about 2^50; exclusion lists must cover this class, not only the weak curves themselves.
Exact evaluation of S_r with r in the input is NP-complete (conditionally for elliptic curves), a warning on large-r summation methods; it does not cover the bounded-root problem at fixed m.
Groebner runs beat the linearization bound by a factor ~2 in the exponent, so the Assumption-1 linearization analysis is an upper estimate, not the actual solver behaviour.
KY measured the degree of regularity rising with n (3 to >= 5 between n = 12 and 45) and found no reasoning supporting any specific slow growth law.
All weak curves have #E = 0 mod 4, so independence can hold only within classes with that cardinality.
General isogenous genus-3 Jacobians exist for any maximal isotropic kernel, but only tractable (Z/2Z)^3 kernels are explicit, so Theorem 2 is a lower estimate.
The quasi-polynomial conclusion no longer depends on the conjecture (the conjecture itself stays open).
The heuristic quasi-polynomial claim is now a theorem in fixed characteristic (with a different algorithm).
Both source and target groups must be priced under their best known attacks.
